descricao_original: Interfascicular oligodendrocytes, the second type, form the myelin sheath around axons in the CNS. Oligodendrocytes have small, dark nuclei compared with the larger, paler nuclei of fibrous astrocytes; the processes of both cells are not seen with routine staining. 1000x

marcadores.explicacao_original: An oligodendrocyte forms multiple internodal segments of myelin on multiple axons, in contrast to a Schwann cell which forms only one internode on one axon. Myelin in the CNS forms in an analogous fashion to that in the PNS, forming concentric wrappings around the axon.
